What this session added — memorization in bilinear layers

A detailed accounting of the results from this session (Parts 1–3 of the memorization post, 2026-08-10/11, code in basis_aligned/memorization_post/) that are not in the prior repo github.com/loganriggs/memorization — with the prior repo's closest result stated alongside each one. Companion to comparison_to_prior_work.md, which also lists the agreements and the prior-only results. Every registered prediction cited below was committed to git before its measurement (predictions/; commit time = registration time).

0. Definitions · 1. Feasibility certificates · 2. The frame taxonomy · 3. Composed-storage decomposition · 4. Capacity as expressivity · 5. Path ≠ entries · 6. Representation-side forecasting · 7. All-inputs audit · 8. Injection & causal component tests · 9. Summary table · 10. Loose ends

0. Definitions (everything used below)

Bilinear layer
y = D((Lx) ∗ (Rx)): input x ∈ ℝd, hidden width H, L and R are H×d, ∗ is the elementwise product over the H hidden units, D maps the H products to the output. Its logits are an exact degree-2 polynomial (quadratic form) in x.
Folded tensor / interaction matrix
T[i,j,c] = Σh D[c,h]·sym(L[h,i]R[h,j]). The slice Bc = T[:,:,c] is class c's d×d interaction matrix: logitc(x) = xTBcx. On boolean inputs xi² = xi, so Bc's diagonal acts as a linear term.
Two-layer model (Part 3)
Residual stream: x₁ = z + B1(z), logits = W(x₁ + B2(x₁)), where B1, B2 are bilinear blocks (width H per block, stream dimension d = 20) and W is a linear readout. The composed function is degree-4 in z. Notation: h₂(z) = (L₂x₁) ∗ (R₂x₁) ∈ ℝH is the last block's hidden representation of key z; G = W·D₂, so logits = W x₁ + G h₂(z).
Fact / key / margin
A fact is a pair (z, y): a random n-bit boolean key z mapped to one of C = 10 class labels y. A fact is memorized when argmax of the logits at z equals y. Its margin is logity(z) − maxc≠y logitc(z) — positive iff memorized, and the distance-to-breaking under perturbations.
Frame
A parameter block in which the logits are exactly linear when all other parameters are held fixed — no Taylor approximation. One layer has frames D, R, L (logits = D h(z) is linear in D; h is linear in R with L fixed, and vice versa). The two-layer model's last block has frames D₂ (equivalently G), R₂, L₂, and W. One layer additionally has the folded-tensor frame: the full coefficient space of the quadratic logit functions, C × 210 numbers at d = 20 (210 = the count of monomials xixj, i ≤ j). Any edit within a frame can be applied to the actual weights and verified exactly.
Load ratio
(number of stored facts) / (frame dimension). E.g. 1200 facts against the 40-dimensional h₂ frame is a 30× load.
KKT edit
The closed-form minimum-norm weight change satisfying linear equality constraints (e.g. "logits at key z* become uniform"), where the norm is weighted by C = Σk (key representation)(key representation)T over the stored facts — so the change is aimed along directions the other stored keys use least. "KKT" because the solution comes from the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions of that constrained minimization; the collateral it causes on every retained fact is computable in closed form before applying it.
Margin LP
A linear program over one frame: equality constraints pin the removed keys' logits at exactly uniform; inequality constraints require every retained fact to keep margin ≥ 0.5; slack variables measure violation, and the objective minimizes total slack. Total slack 0 ⇔ a zero-collateral edit exists in that frame (feasible). Slack > 0 at the optimum is a certificate of impossibility for the entire frame, with the minimum achievable damage quantified.
Alternation / ladder
Solving the margin LP in one frame, applying the edit exactly, then re-solving in the next frame (removal equalities re-imposed each round): G → R₂ → L₂ → … Each round is an exact convex solve; the sequence is coordinate descent across frames.
Retension (prior repo's term)
The prior repo's two-stage editor: a proximal rank-1 delete, then gradient/greedy hinge repair of bystander margins from the post-delete weights with the target pinned negative. Same goal as the margin LP; optimization-based rather than a one-shot convex solve.
Registered prediction
A quantitative prediction with a confidence, committed to git before the measurement runs; the measuring code refuses to run if the prediction file has uncommitted changes. Outcomes are scored confirmed/refuted against the registered bar, not retrofitted.

1 Feasibility certificates: from "our edit failed" to "no edit exists"

Prior repo's closest result. Editing floors were empirical: in the dense toy at crowded load, an oracle search over single rank-1 deletions floored at ~23 broken bystanders (p3), and the two-stage delete-then-retension recipe then reached 0 collateral in every regime tested (t3) — showing the floor was a property of single edits. But "floor" always meant "the best we found by search".
What this session added. The margin LP converts the floor into a proof. In the two-layer model (1200 facts, H = 40 per block), the LP over the last block's output frame is infeasible on all 5 seeds: minimum total hinge violation 5067–5873, with 552–620 retained facts violated at the optimum. That is a certificate that no edit of that entire parameter block — not just the KKT one, not just rank-1 ones — can remove the 10 target facts while keeping all 1190 others at margin ≥ 0.5. The certified floor also calibrates the KKT edit: its ~45% collateral (516–536 flips) matches the LP optimum's 522–578, so the closed-form editor was already essentially optimal within its frame.

The same instrument then mapped the exact editability boundary of a single layer (H = 40, one seed, 10-fact removals, facts trained to 100%): at 350 stored facts the single-frame LP is feasible (0 collateral, one round); at 600 it is infeasible (255 forced breaks at the optimum) but one extra frame-round reaches 0; at 900 the weight-frame alternation stalls (below). Every claim of impossibility in this session is an LP verdict, not a search failure.

2 The frame taxonomy: editability = the affordable linear frame

Prior repo's closest result. Exact closed-form "ledgers" for last-layer edits in the no-norm multilinear transformer (t4): the margin change of every fact under a rank-1 last-layer edit is closed form, and predicted collateral matched reality fact-for-fact. Retension then repaired at depth. The linearity of the last layer was used; a systematic account of which parameter blocks admit exact editing, and what that buys, was not the framing.
What this session added. A taxonomy: enumerate every frame (block whose logits are exactly linear in it), run the same margin LP in each, and alternate. This produced two results the prior repo does not have:

2a. The one-layer / two-layer editability inversion

Near capacity, a single layer is weight-frame uneditable: at 900 facts (22.5× load on its 40-dim frames, still 100% memorized), alternating D → R → L stalls at ~403 broken facts after 7 rounds, violation plateauing. The two-layer model at higher load (1200 facts, 30×) converges cleanly: 522 → 257 → 121 → 118 → 23 → 0 broken facts in 6 rounds, with the 10 removed keys pinned at exactly uniform logits (deviation ~3×10−12, verified by running the edited network). Composition makes the last block's frames richer, not poorer — the D₂/R₂/L₂ frames parameterize different function families because they act through a nonlinear, already-enriched stream.

2b. The folded tensor as one layer's free maximal frame

A single bilinear layer owns a frame that composition destroys: the folded tensor itself — all C × 210 quadratic coefficients, i.e. its entire function space as one linear frame. One margin LP there achieves zero collateral with exact forgetting at 350, 600, and 900 facts alike (verified to 3×10−9 after mapping the coefficients back to a symmetric tensor). So the one-layer weight-frame stall at 900 is a parameterization artifact of coordinate descent in L/R/D — not a function-class limit. The two-layer analog of this maximal frame is the degree-4 coefficient space (~d4 numbers) — unaffordable — which is why the two-layer model must edit in weight frames, and lucky that composition makes them rich enough to converge. One sentence: editability is a property of the affordable linear frame, not of depth or load alone.

3 Composed storage, decomposed: what "cross-layer" means quantitatively

Prior repo's closest result. Storage location was probed by freezing: with width-matched blocks, freezing either one costs nothing below capacity (storage is opportunistic) and 40–50% at saturation (both recruited) — an accuracy-level result (p2/p3). The 6-layer LM work located memorized facts by gradient concentration. Neither decomposes what the composed function is made of.
What this session added. An exact polynomial decomposition of the trained two-layer model on its stored keys: full logits = W z + W B1(z) + W B2(z) + cross, where the first three terms are the degree-≤2 "additive" part (each block evaluated on the raw key) and cross is everything composition creates (degree 3–4). Measured at the capacity-stressed working point (1200 facts, H = 40, 5 seeds):
  • The additive surrogate alone keeps 17–19% of facts — the cross terms carry ~980 of 1200. The median fact has ~98% of its logit magnitude in the cross terms. The composed terms are not a correction; they are the memory.
  • Attribution by single-layer evaluation (positive-controlled: with one block frozen at zero during training, the metric assigns exactly 0 facts to the dead layer): 62–66% of facts are classified correctly by neither single layer, and every other bin sits at the 10% chance floor. Bin names, defined: "either alone (redundant)" = each single layer suffices independently; "needs both (composed)" = no single layer suffices.
  • The draft's "negation for every fact" hunch was tested and refuted (registered at 0.5 confidence): the cosine between the cross-term logit vector and either layer's direct write is a broad distribution centered near zero (medians +0.07…+0.13 for layer 1) — the composition is a nearly orthogonal third channel, not an interference canceller.
  • Ablation asymmetry (registered prediction refuted): zeroing block 1 hurts slightly more than block 2 (block 2 computes on the block-1-enriched stream), both catastrophic (~16–20% survive).

This is consistent with the prior repo's opportunistic-storage law and extends it: below capacity storage is redundant/opportunistic (his freezing result); under stress it becomes composed — not "in layer 1 and layer 2" but in the product structure between them.

4 Capacity as expressivity, pinned exactly

Prior repo's closest result. Careful capacity comparisons: bilinear beats a parameter-matched ReLU MLP (+13–70%), SwiGLU ≈ bilinear, ~2.4–3.1 bits/parameter, scaling ~d1.65–1.7 — trained-search capacities under a fixed protocol. Also the CP/ALS lesson: capacity is about winning argmaxes, not reconstructing the fact tensor.
What this session added. A capacity curve whose plateau is provably the function class. Facts learned from a fixed pool of 4000, one block: 955 at H = 20, then 1022–1026 at every width from 40 to 300 — flat to three digits through H = 210, the exact dimension at which the model's rank-limited quadratic family saturates the full 210-monomial space (so widening past it provably adds nothing). The plateau level also quantifies the argmax-vs-interpolation gap at the function-class level: ~1024 facts stored against 210 monomial coefficients — margin classification is ~5× cheaper than interpolation. Two blocks: 1244 → 1994 → 3522 → 4000 (pool exhausted) at H = 10/20/40/80 — width-limited, never expressivity-limited in range. This is the figure that separates "ran out of parameters" from "ran out of function class" — the prior repo's capacities cannot make that separation because trained ReLU search has no analytic expressivity boundary to pin to.

5 A path is not a set of tensor entries (Part 1, F8/F8b)

Prior repo's closest result. The margins thesis throughout ("facts are stored as margins"), and mechanism work on how sparse models encode facts (silence codes, signed cancellations). No experiment attempts to remove a computation path by zeroing its interaction entries.
What this session added. A direct test that sharpens the margins thesis into a negative about weight surgery. Setup: 3 classes over features [furry, happy, whiskers, tail]; Dog = furry∧happy or happy∧tail; Cat = furry∧whiskers or whiskers∧tail. Goal: remove the (happy,tail)→Dog path without touching the other four stored patterns. Three registered rounds:
  • Zeroing the (happy,tail) interaction entry exactly (preserving (furry,happy) exactly): the {happy,tail} input is still classified Dog on 5/5 seeds — the boolean diagonal terms co-carry the path.
  • Zeroing every tail-involving entry of Dog's slice (registered at 0.65 confidence that this would work): still no flip, 0/5 — the (happy,happy) diagonal, shared with the kept furry∧happy path, alone outscores the competitors. There is no set of tensor entries whose removal removes this fact without breaking shared structure.
  • The functional key-frame edit (constrain the logit on the stored key itself: set fDog(zhappy,tail) below the best competitor, preserve fDog(zfurry,happy) exactly): flips the target 5/5 with zero collateral when overcomplete — while the (happy,tail) tensor entry remains visibly nonzero. The behavior was removed without touching "its" entry.

Bonus asymmetry: in the undercomplete model (H = 3) the full-tail edit is not even expressible (5 exact constraints against 3 free parameters in Dog's readout row) — and the same functional edit that is surgical when overcomplete drags Cat keys to Dog on 3/5 seeds there. A fact is a margin relation among stored keys, not a location in the weight tensor.

6 Pre-registered, representation-side collateral forecasting

Prior repo's closest result. Two forecasting results: (i) exact post-hoc ledgers for last-layer edits (collateral predicted fact-for-fact given the edit); (ii) t3c's pre-edit neighbor retrieval from weights alone — top singular directions of the edit's function change — which reached AUC 0.56–0.71 but lost to the raw input-overlap baseline |xi·xk| (AUC 0.63–0.75), diagnosed as "breaking = interference × slack" (a weights-side score can't see slack). At depth, activation-overlap shortlists collapsed to precision ≈ 0.
What this session added. The representation-side forecaster, with pre-registration discipline. The stored-key Gram — cosines between the model's own hidden representations of its stored keys, hk = (Lzk) ∗ (Rzk) — predicts measured collateral of KKT edits at r = 0.943 / Spearman 0.931 across 60 (edit, victim) pairs, with every predicted value committed to git before measurement (C1/F6). The KKT edit's own collateral prediction is exact (r = 1.000000, F11) because the edit is linear in its frame. The regime contrast is itself forecast: undercomplete collateral ~3.7× overcomplete. Where the prior repo's weights-side score under-performed its baseline, the hidden-representation Gram works — consistent with his own diagnosis, since the Gram measures interference where it acts (in representation space), and the margin LP then supplies the slack half exactly.

The discipline itself is also an addition: every measurement in Parts 1–3 (16 registered predictions, P1–P16c plus the Part-1 rounds) was gated on a committed prediction file, and the score was 9 confirmed / 5 refuted / 2 moot — the refutations (negation hunch, ablation asymmetry, one-layer editability-to-capacity) are reported as prominently as the confirmations.

7 An all-inputs behavior audit (F12)

Prior repo's closest result. Margin distributions and margin-based auditing everywhere (quantization fragility, normalized margins), evaluated on the stored facts and held-out sets — never on the entire input space, and with no analytic guarantee attached.
What this session added. The exhaustive check: all 220 inputs evaluated against the analytic Gram-overlap bound |fc(x)| ≤ 2·maxk|λck|· xTC−1x (+ residual term). The bound holds everywhere but is 35–55× loose; and ~20% of off-fact inputs carry a larger top1–top2 margin than the least-confident stored fact for the SGD and ALS models (1.4% for the minimum-norm KKT interpolant). Consequence for both write-ups: "behavior guaranteed on all 2n inputs" can only be claimed as the bound itself; the off-distribution confidence landscape of a memorizer is genuinely non-small, and only the minimum-norm interpolant is well-behaved off-distribution.

8 Injection at scale, and causal (not spectral) evidence against per-fact components

Prior repo's closest result. Certified insertion in toys — including the gameability result (785 facts stored as ±10−9 argmax ties at d16, showing capacity criteria need margin floors). Superposition evidence was spectral/statistical: effective rank, participation ratios, no-zero-activation codes.
What this session added. Two things. Injection into a trained composed model: 10 brand-new facts inserted by one closed-form least-norm edit in the h₂ frame, landing 10/10 exactly on every seed, with measured collateral 218–390 of 1200 stored facts (~18–32%) — cheaper than removal (~45%), quantifying a removal/injection asymmetry in the crowded regime. A causal test for per-fact components: decompose the readout over a dictionary of per-fact directions, then delete each fact's component and watch what breaks. Answer: nothing — 0/1200 own-fact breaks, 0.0% median collateral. Each "component" is weightless. (En route, the naive metric — "does a fact's component classify its own key?" — was caught returning a degenerate ~100%: with 1200 dictionary atoms in a 40-dim frame it just reproduces a whitened copy of the full model's logits. The bug was caught by asking what the null would produce, before any claim.) Facts in the composed regime are functionally present but nowhere located — and section 2 shows they are nonetheless exactly removable. Location and editability come apart in both directions.

10 Loose ends this comparison opens

  • Run the attribution bins on a sub-capacity two-layer model (e.g. 300 facts at H = 40): prediction, the "either alone (redundant)" bin dominates — closing the loop with the prior repo's opportunistic-storage law.
  • Re-run the capacity curve with a margin floor (the prior repo's gameability result says bare-argmax capacity is gameable; the plateau should persist but the honest curve needs the floor).
  • Measure total weight change ‖ΔW‖ for the alternating-frame edits — the prior repo's retension costs 10–20× the delete-only change; the LP edits' cost is unmeasured.
  • Head-to-head pre-edit forecasters on one model: prior t3c's weights-side shortlist → forward-margin confirmation vs the stored-key Gram.
